venue.name: WildPlay Element Parks Victoria
venue.description: WildPlay Victoria is an outdoor aerial adventure park in the trees beside the Q Centre in Colwood, about 15 minutes from downtown Victoria. It has three treetop obstacle courses, a six flight zipline tour, a 40 foot freefall jump and an axe throwing range, all run by certified guides who fit the harnesses and coach from the ground. School field trips are taken on the Kids Course and the Classic Course for groups of 15 or more, at published per student rates. Every activity has a minimum age, and most also have a minimum height or weight, so the numbers matter more here than at most venues. WildPlay runs six parks in Canada and the United States; everything recorded here is the Victoria park only.

facility_notes.lunch_space: Snacks and drinks are available at Guest Services, and there are picnic tables on site. We recommend every student brings a water bottle.
facility_notes.rain_backup: Courses run in light rain. If conditions become unsafe we close, and your group is rescheduled or fully refunded.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Free parking on site. Follow the signage down to the Q Centre arena and look for WildPlay's entrance at the end of the parking lot, next to the Velodrome.

venue.nearby_park: WildPlay is located near the Galloping Goose trail. Bicycle racks are available next to Guest Services and at Westshore Rec Centre. There are walking trails in the park.
restrictions: Every student needs a WildPlay waiver signed by a parent or guardian.
Students 13 and under must have a responsible adult on site.
Kids Adventure Course: ages 5 and up, must be 114 cm (3'9") tall, maximum weight 300 lbs.
Classic and Extreme Adventure Courses: ages 5 and up, must be 142 cm (4'8") tall, maximum weight 300 lbs.
What's To Fear Jump: ages 5 and up, must weigh 44 lbs (20 kg), maximum weight 285 lbs.
Zipline Tours: ages 7 and up. Participants under 100 lbs (46 kg) ride tandem with a guide. Maximum weight 300 lbs.
Closed toe shoes that are secured to the foot, so no flip flops, sandals or slides. Long hair tied back and jewellery left at home.
Guests must be in good health and not subject to dizziness or motion sickness, must be free from high blood pressure, heart, back or neck problems, and must not be pregnant.
Smoking is not permitted around the elements or in the forest, and there is zero tolerance for alcohol and drugs.
venue.hours_notes: 2026 hours. July 1 to September 7: seven days a week, 9am to 8pm. September 8 to October 5: Thursday to Monday, 10am to 6pm. October 6 to October 31: Friday to Monday, 10am to 6pm. November 1 to December 13: Saturday and Sunday, 10am to 4pm.
venue.seasonal_notes: Published hours run to December 13. Group bookings are available on non-operational days by request.

programs.name: School field trip, Kids Course
programs.description: A field trip on the Kids Course, for school groups of 15 or more on the same course. The course is a single level reaching up to 15 feet and is built for children between 5 and 12. The minimum height is 3 feet 9 inches, or 114 cm, and children shorter than the 4 foot 8 inch mark needed for the Classic Course can take part on this one whatever their age. Groups are often split across the two courses and the group host helps work out the numbers. The course itself takes 45 to 90 minutes and they say to plan on a half day for a group. The rate is from $22.99 a student plus tax and is lowest Monday to Thursday, which is when most school groups come. Large changes in numbers need three days notice and changes of one or two students need 24 hours.
programs.what_children_do: Get fitted with a harness on the ground and learn how the continuous belay works, then climb up into the trees and make their way from tree to tree across tightropes, cargo nets, wobbly bridges, rope swings and short ziplines, choosing their own route and stopping when they want to.
programs.our_note: Height decides this more than age does. A child under 4 foot 8 goes on this course whatever year they are in, so measure before you split the class. Midweek is cheaper. No washroom is listed anywhere on their site, which is worth a phone call before you take a group of five year olds.
programs.practical_summary: It is all outdoors, with free parking, picnic tables and snacks for sale at Guest Services. There is no indoor alternative, they run in light rain and close and reschedule if it turns unsafe, and washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Rates are lowest Monday to Thursday. The published figure is a from price, so the day you pick changes it.
programs.cancellation_note: Large changes in numbers need at least three days notice and changes of one or two students need 24 hours. Groups of 15 or more may be subject to different cancellation terms and should call to reschedule.
programs.evidence: Rates start at $22.99 per student on the Kids Course and $34.99 on the Classic Course, plus tax

programs.name: School field trip, Classic Course
programs.description: A field trip on the Classic Course, for school groups of 15 or more on the same course, ages 5 to 18. The course has three levels of obstacles that get higher and harder as students work up it, and the whole run takes 90 to 120 minutes. The minimum height is 4 feet 8 inches, or 142 cm, and the maximum weight is 300 lbs. Students shorter than that go on the Kids Course instead, and groups are often split across both. The rate is from $34.99 a student plus tax and is lowest Monday to Thursday. They say to plan on a half day, with the exact timing worked out by the group host once they know the numbers and arrival time.
programs.what_children_do: Train on the ground first, then climb a ladder into the trees and work along tightropes, cargo nets, swinging logs and ziplines, moving up through three levels as they get more confident. Guides walk underneath and talk anyone who freezes through the next bit, or bring them down.
programs.our_note: Students choose their own route and can stop whenever they like, which is the part nervous children need telling in advance. Ask the group host to confirm how many adults you need, because that is not published and it will shape your parent helper list. Book Monday to Thursday if the budget is tight.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors from start to finish, with picnic tables, snacks for sale and free parking at the Q Centre. No wet weather alternative and no washrooms mentioned on the site, so both are worth asking about when you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: Rates are lowest Monday to Thursday. The published figure is a from price, so the day you pick changes it.
programs.cancellation_note: Large changes in numbers need at least three days notice and changes of one or two students need 24 hours. Groups of 15 or more may be subject to different cancellation terms and should call to reschedule.
programs.evidence: Adventure Course field trips for school groups of 15+. Ages 5 to 18, from $22.99 per student.

gaps: Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site, including the park's own list of what is on site. For a group of young children this is the first thing to ask about.
How many adults have to come is not published. They say the group host sorts that out with you when you book.
No coordinates are published, so the street address needs geocoding before the map and the travel time will work.
Months are unknown. The only published hours run from July to mid December in 2026, so it is not clear from the site whether a school group can come in spring.
How long a group visit takes is not published beyond planning on a half day. The courses themselves are given as 45 to 90 minutes for the Kids Course and 90 to 120 minutes for the Classic Course.
Nothing is published about bus parking or a coach drop off, only that parking is free and on site at the Q Centre.
There is no minimum notice published for booking a school group. They say a group host usually replies within one business day.
Prices for the zipline tour, the axe throwing and ordinary adventure course visits are only shown inside the booking system, not on the park page, so they are not recorded here.
The picture the site offers for sharing on the Victoria page is a promotional giveaway graphic rather than a photograph, so the main photo here was taken from the park page instead.
wildplay.com covers six parks. The address, hours and the school rates recorded here are the Victoria park only.
